svg.title: Traditional user decision loop compared with an agentic machine loop
svg.desc: The traditional application waits for the user after each bounded request. An agentic application turns one delegated goal into concurrent model, tool, and verification loops before returning completed work.

g.text: One request waits for a person; one goal can launch a work tree
The pacing mechanism changes from human decisions to machine feedback loops.
The user stays in the decision loop
One decision → one bounded operation → pause
The user delegates a goal; the machine stays in the execution loop
Concurrent branches continue without waiting for another user action.
Infrastructure efficiency compounds across the whole work tree
